Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x,\,y+2z,\,z-2y⟩$ and the boundary $S$ of a spherical solid of radius $\sqrt{3}$ centered at the origin. Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S.$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

For a sphere or radius $r$ centered at $O,$ the unit normal to the sphere is given by

$$
n=\frac{⟨x,y,z⟩}{r}.
$$

In our case, we have $r=\sqrt{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
n=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨x,y,z⟩.
$$

Using the fact that ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=3$ on $S,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨x,\,y+2z,\,z-2y⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨x,\,y+2z,\,z-2y⟩\cdot ⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}({x}^{2}+y(y+2z)+z(z-2y)) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2yz+{z}^{2}-2yz) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot 3 \\  & =\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}\sqrt{3}\,\text{d}S \\  & =\sqrt{3}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot \text{Area}(S) \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot 4\pi \cdot (\sqrt{3})^{2} \\  & =12\pi \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$
